takeaways: Energy drinks/stimulants vs. products without: 11× cardiac arrest reports, 4.5× heart attack reports

title: United States at risk of losing measles elimination status due to ongoing outbreaks
summary: The United States faces potential loss of its measles elimination status following recent outbreaks. A WHO regional committee is expected to decide this week whether the U.S. retains the status it achieved in 2000.
takeaways: At least 8 measles deaths reported in 2026
Decision expected from Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) committee this week
Loss of status previously described as unavoidable consequence of transmission patterns

title: Amyloid Removal in Alzheimer's Brain Shows Protective Effect on Tau

takeaways: Brain regions cleared of amyloid plaques showed little or no tau buildup
Neighboring areas still containing amyloid showed much higher tau levels
Study presented at 2026 Alzheimer's Association International Conference and published in JAMA
Donanemab (Kisunla) and lecanemab (Leqembi) received full FDA approval for amyloid-targeting

title: Stroke Rates Nearly Double Among Younger Adults Over Three Decades
summary: Stroke rates among adults ages 20 to 54 nearly doubled over three decades in the Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky region, rising 83% from 33.9 cases per 100,000 person-years in 1993–1994 to 62.2 in 2020. takeaways: Stroke rates rose 83% from 1993–1994 to 2020 in young adults aged 20–54
Ischemic strokes rose from 23.8 to 47.3 cases per 100,000 person-years
2,076 adults experienced first stroke during study period spanning 1993–2020
Associations with hypertension, diabetes, and substance use identified
Study published September 23, 2026 in Neurology journal

title: New injectable treatment for knee arthritis shows 80% pain relief lasting 12 months
summary: A new injectable treatment using genicular artery embolization (GAE) delivered clinically meaningful knee pain relief to 80% of 194 patients for at least 12 months without surgery. takeaways: 80% of 194 patients achieved clinically meaningful pain relief for ≥12 months

Minimally invasive alternative for patients exhausting physical therapy, medication, and joint injections
Avoids joint replacement surgery
Knee osteoarthritis affects 365+ million adults worldwide per WHO

title: All of Us study identifies thousands of new genetic variants affecting drug response
summary: The All of Us study, conducted using data from the National Institutes of Health's All of Us program, analyzed nearly 100,000 Americans and identified thousands of new genetic variants in 16 pharmacogenes that influence responses to prescription drugs. title: Occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher stroke risk
summary: A study of 440,000+ Americans presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026 found occasional marijuana use associated with 40% higher odds of reporting stroke history. The association held across consumption methods and was not limited to frequent users.
takeaways: Occasional cannabis use: 40% higher stroke history odds
Study population: 440,000+ Americans (BRFSS data 2020–2024)
U.S. cannabis use surge: 1 in 6 adults in 2024 vs. 1 in 10 in 2020 (51% increase)
Association established, causation not proven; affects all consumption methods

title: Bioengineered chewing gum reduces HPV levels by up to 93% in cancer patients
summary: University of Pennsylvania scientists developed a bioengineered chewing gum containing plant-based proteins that reduced HPV levels by up to 93% in laboratory tests using oral samples from head and neck cancer patients. takeaways: HPV reduction: up to 93% in lab tests on patient oral samples
Bacterial impact: nearly eliminated Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum; preserved beneficial oral bacteria
HPV, Pg, Fn linked to oropharyngeal cancer development and worsened survival
Published in Scientific Reports
Potential for affordable treatment supporting cancer prevention and existing therapies

summary: A major study found that 16 of 22 cancer types rose significantly in younger women aged 20–49 between 2001 and 2019, and 11 of 21 cancers in younger men—a trend that persists despite improvements in smoking, diet, and other established risk factors. takeaways: 16 of 22 cancers increased significantly in younger women; 11 of 21 in younger men
Bowel and ovarian cancers rose only in younger adults, not older age groups
Excess body weight cannot fully account for the observed increases
Study analyzed England data from 2001–2019 across 20+ cancer types

summary: Rutgers University researchers published findings in Annals of Internal Medicine linking GLP-1 receptor agonists—including semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound)—to a modestly increased risk of ischemic optic neuropathy, a rare condition causing sudden and potentially per
takeaways: Ozempic, Wegovy (semaglutide) and Mounjaro, Zepbound (tirzepatide) linked to ischemic optic neuropathy
Risk increase: ~3–4 additional cases per 10,000 patients over 18 months
Condition causes sudden vision loss; more common in men and adults 50–65
Study analyzed large US database of Type 2 diabetes patients ages 18–65

title: U.S. science leaders warn shifting research funding from universities to industry risks basic research drought
summary: U.S. science leaders including MIT President Sally Kornbluth warn that the White House's planned shift of research funding from universities to industry threatens basic scientific research. MIT graduate admissions fell nearly 20% to 500 fewer students in fall 2026 due to a $100 million federal resea
takeaways: MIT graduate enrollment dropped 20%: ~500 fewer students fall 2026 vs. 2024
$100 million federal research award cut attributed to MIT enrollment decline
Universities cutting graduate admissions due to 18-month period of grant terminations and delays
Kornbluth warned of 'serious drought' in curiosity-driven research

title: Brain Remains Active Under Anesthesia, Analyzing Language
summary: Baylor researchers discovered that the human brain processes language and predicts upcoming words even under general anesthesia, challenging assumptions about consciousness. Using neural recordings from the hippocampus, they found neurons responding differently to unexpected sounds and demonstrating
takeaways: Neurons showed improved ability to distinguish unusual tones over time
Brain demonstrates neural plasticity without conscious awareness
Research used Neuropixels probes recording from hundreds of individual neurons in hippocampus
Findings published in Nature
Discovery could advance communication technologies for neurologically injured patients

title: Small Cancer Cells with Extra Chromosomes Show Higher Aggression
summary: Virginia Tech researchers discovered that unusually small cancer cells carrying extra chromosomes grow faster, spread more readily, and resist common treatments. The five-year study involved creating tetraploid cancer cells with four complete chromosome sets and examining tumor behavior in mice.
takeaways: Small cancer cells with extra chromosomes grow faster and spread more readily
Tetraploid cells contain four complete sets of chromosomes instead of normal two
Extra chromosomes common characteristic of cancer found in study
Findings published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences and Cancer Research
Research conducted over five years examining tumors in mice

title: Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case
summary: Kenya reported a second Ebola case as the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to struggle with over 4,000 deaths and 9,000 confirmed cases.

title: Scientists find fructose may enable aggressive ovarian cancer cells to spread
summary: Researchers discovered that fructose, commonly found in sweetened foods, may help chemotherapy-resistant ovarian cancer cells weaken tumor cell bonds and metastasize.

title: Biogen Expects Pivotal Lupus Trial Readout
summary: Biogen is preparing to release results from pivotal clinical trials of an experimental lupus therapy.

title: Obesity paradox: overweight dementia patients show 16–27% lower mortality
summary: A study of 4,500+ older adults found that overweight and obese individuals diagnosed with dementia had 16–27% lower death risk than normal-weight peers, possibly due to greater metabolic reserves.

title: Preventive Care Panel Members Hold Significant Pharma and Medical Practice Financial Interests
summary: Federal filings reveal that US Preventive Services Task Force panelists hold substantial conflicts of interest including pharma stocks and private practices, despite ethics waivers.

title: Drug companies explore workarounds to protect U.S. sales amid president's most-favored-nations drug pricing policy
summary: Pharmaceutical manufacturers are developing strategies to shield domestic revenues in response to the president's most-favored-nations policy affecting drug pricing.

title: Alternative BMI metrics could flip obesity diagnosis for millions
summary: A newly proposed obesity identification method could reclassify millions of people, potentially enabling more targeted medical care.

title: 47-year study reveals age 35 as turning point for physical strength decline
summary: A 47-year longitudinal study found that fitness and strength begin declining around age 35 even among regularly exercising people, though exercise begun in adulthood can still improve outcomes.

title: Late-Night Eating Linked to 30% Higher Liver Disease Risk
summary: A study of nearly 200,000 people found that eating late at night or around bedtime increased liver disease risk by 20–30%.

title: Former FDA officials criticize DOGE cuts as catastrophic to agency capacity
summary: Three former FDA chiefs condemned DOGE-driven cuts, warning the agency has lost institutional knowledge that will take years to restore.

title: Study finds popular workout recovery techniques often overstated or counterproductive
summary: Research shows ice baths, massages, and compression garments provide limited benefits and may undermine long-term muscle gains, while simple recovery methods prove most effective.

title: UC Santa Cruz research highlights overlooked peptide P3 as potential Alzheimer's culprit
summary: Researchers draw attention to a largely overlooked peptide called P3 that may play a significant role in Alzheimer's disease, after decades of focus on amyloid beta proved disappointing.

title: Scientists discover protein that helps senescent cells evade immune detection
summary: Research identifies a protein that allows aging senescent cells to hide from the immune system, with blocking the protein in mice reducing these harmful cells and improving metabolic function.

title: Study Examines GLP-1 Weight Loss Drugs' Impact on Criminal Justice, Employment, and Housing Outcomes
summary: A clinical trial announced results examining how GLP-1 weight loss medications affect substance use disorders and downstream social outcomes including criminal justice involvement and housing stability.

title: Trump administration delays rule restricting imported prescription medicines
summary: The Trump administration is postponing a federal rule by 90 days that could prevent Americans from purchasing prescription drugs from licensed international pharmacies.

title: Study: high-intensity sports with explosive movements more effective than walking or weight training for bone strength
summary: A study suggests that walking and weight training alone may not adequately maintain bone strength.

title: MDCalc Launches CrossCover Tool to Help Doctors Verify AI Medical Chatbot Answers
summary: MDCalc introduces CrossCover, a verification tool designed to increase clinician confidence in generative AI medical reference systems.

title: Healthcare Providers Sue Employers Over Out-of-Network Medical Bill Disputes
summary: Medical providers increasingly pursue legal action against employers, claiming responsibility for out-of-network bills insurers have delayed or underpaid.

title: Lobbyists and medical trade groups shape state AI regulation policy
summary: Hospital and physician lobby groups are working behind the scenes to influence how states regulate artificial intelligence in medical applications.

title: FDA advisory committee members' industry ties face scrutiny in new research
summary: New research reveals that nearly 40% of FDA advisory committee meetings over a 20-year period included patient or consumer representatives with active ties to advocacy groups funded by industry.
takeaways: Nearly 40% of FDA advisory meetings had patient/consumer reps with pharma-linked ties
Over 50% of some committees included such representatives
>10% of meetings had rep from group funded by reviewed drugmaker
Most organizational ties were not disclosed at meetings
FDA conflict policies less developed for patient/consumer reps than scientific advisors

title: Pharma bro Martin Shkreli faces contempt charges for violating industry ban
summary: The FTC asked a U.S. court to hold Martin Shkreli in contempt for allegedly violating a court order that prohibits him from working in the pharmaceutical industry.

title: Startup Radical Numerics pursues 'general biological intelligence' using AI
summary: Radical Numerics, led by CEO Eric Nguyen, is building AI systems targeting general biological intelligence, representing a new frontier in AI applications.

title: Alnylam's Amvuttra Heart Drug Faces Sales Slowdown, Threatening Biotech Growth
summary: Alnylam, once positioned to reach $100 billion valuation, is struggling as sales of its heart drug Amvuttra decelerate.

title: Newly elected doctors and scientists aim to restore public trust in science
summary: Scores of doctors and scientists were elected to office last week, raising hopes they can help rebuild public confidence in scientific institutions.

title: Childhood exercise adapts bodies for easier adult fitness, guinea fowl study suggests
summary: Research on guinea fowl reveals that early physical activity during development may reduce exercise difficulty later in life.

title: Opinion: Incoming Governors Must Prioritize Kindergarten Vaccination Tracking
summary: Public health leaders urge new governors to immediately assess county-level kindergarten vaccination rates as a critical first-day priority.

title: Analysis: MAHA's Relationship with Black Americans Is Complex Despite Activist Rhetoric
summary: Researchers note that Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Make America Healthy Again movement have adopted Black activist language while undermining Black American interests.
